basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 37:9 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 254. Quomodo impletum somnium Joseph, quo dicit se vidisse solem et lunam, et'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 254. Quomodo impletum somnium Joseph, quo dicit se vidisse solem et lunam, et undecim stellas adorasse se (Gen. XXXVII, 9); dum constat, eo regnante in Aegypto, matrem ejus Rachel multo ante esse defunctam; imo nec patrem [ejus] legimus eum adorasse?-- Resp. [Ergo] in Christo facilius [ Edit., facile] est somnii intelligere perfectionem: huic enim datum est nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine ejus [Ms., Jesu] flectatur omne genu coelestium, terrestrium et infernorum (Philip. II, 10).
